concepts.note: Gas pressure gradients balance gravity in a stable star, dP/dr = -Gm(r)ρ/r².
concepts.title: Hydrostatic equilibrium

concepts.note: Radiation pressure sets a maximum stable luminosity, L_Edd = 4πGMm_p c/σ_T.
concepts.title: Eddington luminosity

concepts.note: The pp chain and CNO cycle convert hydrogen to helium and power main-sequence stars.
concepts.title: Hydrogen fusion chains

concepts.note: The 1957 B²FH paper built elements up to iron by fusion, with heavier nuclei made by slow neutron capture (s-process) in stars and rapid neutron capture (r-process) in explosive events; the 2017 kilonova GW170817 confirmed r-process production in neutron-star mergers.
concepts.title: B²FH stellar nucleosynthesis

subtopics.note: Eddington's 1926 models treated stars as gas spheres in hydrostatic equilibrium, with energy carried outward by radiation, and Bethe identified the fusion reactions that power them in 1939. The 1957 B²FH paper explained how stars synthesize elements up to iron and, via neutron capture, beyond it.
subtopics.title: Stellar structure and nucleosynthesis

concepts.note: The present expansion rate, measured near 70 km/s/Mpc, with a persistent discrepancy between distance-ladder and early-universe determinations.
concepts.title: Hubble constant H₀

concepts.note: Cepheid variables and standard candles calibrate extragalactic distances step by step.
concepts.title: Distance ladder

concepts.note: In 1927 Lemaître derived v = H₀d and interpreted it as cosmic expansion, before Hubble's paper.
concepts.title: Lemaître's expanding universe

concepts.note: Cosmological redshift of galaxy spectra grows with distance, a signature of metric expansion.
concepts.title: Redshift-distance relation

subtopics.note: Hubble's 1929 observations showed that galaxy recession velocity grows linearly with distance, v = H₀d, evidence for an expanding universe. Lemaître had derived the relation and its expansion interpretation two years earlier.
subtopics.title: Hubble law

concepts.note: Zwicky inferred far more cluster mass than visible light suggested from galaxy velocity dispersions.
concepts.title: Coma cluster mass discrepancy

concepts.note: Orbital speeds stay roughly constant at large galactic radii, implying dark matter halos.
concepts.title: Flat rotation curves

concepts.note: Galaxies and clusters show M/L far above values expected from stars alone.
concepts.title: Mass-to-light ratios

concepts.note: In 2006 gravitational lensing showed the mass concentrated apart from the hot shocked gas in the colliding cluster 1E 0657-56, strong direct evidence for dark matter.
concepts.title: Bullet Cluster

subtopics.note: Zwicky (1933) found that galaxies in the Coma cluster move too fast for its visible mass, and Rubin and Ford (1970s) measured flat rotation curves in spiral galaxies. Both imply large amounts of non-luminous matter, with v² = GM(r)/r requiring M(r) ∝ r at large radii.
subtopics.title: Dark matter evidence

concepts.note: White dwarfs above roughly 1.4 M_sun cannot be supported by electron degeneracy pressure.
concepts.title: Chandrasekhar limit

concepts.note: Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish discovered pulsars in 1967, confirming neutron stars supported by degeneracy pressure.
concepts.title: Neutron stars and pulsars

concepts.note: The first relativistic model of gravitational collapse forming a black hole.
concepts.title: Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse

concepts.note: Its 2019 radio image of M87*'s shadow gave direct evidence for a supermassive black hole, followed by an image of Sgr A* in 2022.
concepts.title: Event Horizon Telescope

subtopics.note: Chandrasekhar's 1931 limit showed that white dwarfs above about 1.4 solar masses must collapse, and Oppenheimer and Snyder (1939) modeled continued collapse to a black hole. The Event Horizon Telescope imaged the shadow of M87* in 2019, confirming the black-hole picture.
subtopics.title: Compact stars and black holes

concepts.note: The 1948 calculation of primordial element abundances in a hot Big Bang.
concepts.title: Alpher-Bethe-Gamow paper

concepts.note: Weak interactions decouple near 1 MeV, fixing the neutron-to-proton ratio at about 1/7.
concepts.title: Neutron-proton freeze-out

concepts.note: Deuterium formation waits until the temperature falls to about 0.1 MeV, starting nucleosynthesis.
concepts.title: Deuterium bottleneck

concepts.note: Predicted H, D, ³He, ⁴He and ⁷Li abundances broadly match observation, with a lingering lithium problem.
concepts.title: Primordial abundances

subtopics.note: Alpher, Bethe and Gamow (1948) showed that the hot early universe synthesized light nuclei, predicting roughly 25% helium by mass. Alpher and Herman also predicted the relic radiation left over from that epoch.
subtopics.title: Big Bang nucleosynthesis

concepts.note: The accidental 1965 detection of isotropic 2.7 K microwave noise at Bell Labs.
concepts.title: Penzias-Wilson discovery

concepts.note: The 1990 FIRAS measurement matched a Planck spectrum to extraordinary precision, T = 2.725 K.
concepts.title: COBE blackbody spectrum

concepts.note: WMAP and Planck map temperature anisotropies and pin down cosmological parameters.
concepts.title: CMB acoustic peaks

concepts.note: Neutral atoms formed near redshift z ≈ 1100, letting photons free-stream to us.
concepts.title: Recombination and decoupling

subtopics.note: Penzias and Wilson detected an unexpected isotropic 2.7 K microwave background in 1965, quickly interpreted by Dicke's group as relic radiation from the hot Big Bang. COBE's FIRAS measured its blackbody spectrum in 1990 and its DMR found the tiny anisotropies in 1992 that seed structure.
subtopics.title: Cosmic microwave background

concepts.note: Regions of the CMB farther apart than the causal horizon nonetheless share the same temperature.
concepts.title: Horizon problem

concepts.note: Inflation drives the density parameter Ω toward 1, explaining the near-flat geometry.
concepts.title: Flatness problem

concepts.note: A scalar field rolling slowly gives near-exponential expansion, a(t) ∝ e^{Ht}, and density perturbations.
concepts.title: Slow-roll inflation

concepts.note: An open search for inflationary gravitational waves imprinted on CMB polarization.
concepts.title: Primordial B-modes

subtopics.note: Starobinsky (1980) and Guth (1981) proposed a brief exponential expansion that solves the horizon and flatness problems and seeds cosmic structure. Linde, Albrecht and Steinhardt developed the slow-roll variants in 1982.
subtopics.title: Cosmic inflation

concepts.note: High-redshift Type Ia supernovae reveal that cosmic expansion is speeding up.
concepts.title: Accelerating universe (1998)

concepts.note: Vacuum energy with negative pressure, obeying w = p/ρc² ≈ -1, drives the acceleration.
concepts.title: Cosmological constant Λ

concepts.note: A six-parameter model with cold dark matter and Λ fits CMB, BAO and supernova data, H² = 8πGρ/3 + Λc²/3 - kc²/a².
concepts.title: ΛCDM model

concepts.note: The 2005 SDSS and 2dFGRS detections of the ~150 Mpc BAO feature provided a standard ruler for mapping the expansion history.
concepts.title: Baryon acoustic oscillations

subtopics.note: In 1998 two supernova teams found distant Type Ia supernovae fainter than expected, implying accelerating expansion driven by dark energy with equation of state w ≈ -1. ΛCDM now fits CMB, supernova and BAO data, although local and early-universe H₀ measurements disagree.
subtopics.title: Dark energy and ΛCDM
